mechanical_arm.valid_contact_strategy: One gripper clamps the upper body of the remote firmly. The second gripper pinches the edges of the battery cover (or uses suction if available, though pinching is better for sliding) and translates linearly downwards.
mechanical_arm.invalid_contact_strategy: Gripping the entire remote with one arm and trying to pull the cover with the same arm; gripping the cover too tightly and crushing it; sliding in the wrong direction (upwards).

dexterous_hand.valid_contact_strategy: Fingers wrap around the remote body for stabilization. Thumb and index finger of the other hand (or same hand if dexterous enough, though bimanual is shown) pinch the textured area of the cover and slide it down.
dexterous_hand.invalid_contact_strategy: Using a power grasp on the cover that prevents sliding; touching only the smooth top surface of the cover without enough friction to slide it.

contact_spec.notes_for_m3_judge: Pay attention to the distinct roles of the two hands: one must stabilize the body while the other slides the cover. The sliding motion must be linear and along the axis of the remote. The cover should not be lifted off (pulled away) but slid along the tracks.

dexterous_hand.valid_contact_strategy: One hand uses fingers to wrap around the padlock body for stability. The other hand uses a precision pinch grasp (thumb-index) on the key head to turn it, then transitions to a power grasp on the shackle to pull.
dexterous_hand.invalid_contact_strategy: Using a single hand to hold the body, turn the key, and pull the shackle simultaneously (requires too many degrees of freedom). Contacting the key shaft instead of the handle (insufficient torque leverage).

contact_spec.notes_for_m3_judge: Pay attention to the sequence: grasp -> turn -> pull -> separate. The key turning must happen before the shackle is pulled. contact_spec.notes_for_m3_judge: Pay attention to the rolling motion: the tool must maintain contact with the fabric surface while moving. The t-shirt must not be dragged or displaced significantly; the left hand's stabilizing role is crucial. The roller should rotate as it moves.

mechanical_arm.valid_contact_strategy: Use parallel jaw gripper to grasp the top or side edges of the sponge firmly. Apply downward force (Z-axis) to maintain contact friction during the wiping trajectory.
mechanical_arm.invalid_contact_strategy: Grasping the bottom cleaning surface of the sponge, or grasping too loosely causing the sponge to slip during the lateral wiping motion.

dexterous_hand.valid_contact_strategy: Wrap fingers around the top and sides of the sponge (power grasp) to distribute pressure evenly across the bottom surface for effective wiping.
dexterous_hand.invalid_contact_strategy: Pinching only a small corner of the sponge with fingertips, which would result in unstable contact and uneven pressure on the table surface.

contact_spec.notes_for_m3_judge: Focus on the continuous contact between the sponge bottom and table surface during the wiping phase (frames 7-25).
